correctness.reason: For the named unit square, Pick's theorem gives no interior lattice point and all four sides have lattice length one. Area and incidence counting force 14 remaining unimodular triangles, 15 dual vertices and 17 bounded dual edges, hence genus 3. Lee–Len Theorem 4.4 then gives seven bitangent classes of multiplicity one and no multiplicity-two class. The package's explicit lower-hull witness is consistent with these counts.
risks: The conclusion is scoped to the stated unit-square subdivision; other genus-dropping nodal quartics are not covered.

originality.reason: Lee–Len Theorem 4.4 already states that every genus-3 tropical plane quartic has seven equivalence classes of bitangent lines, each of multiplicity one. Once the elementary genus-3 count for this unit-square subdivision is made, the headline nonexistence claim is a direct specialization of that published theorem.
risks: The exact height vector for this particular regular subdivision may be new as data, but it does not rescue originality of the final claim.

value.reason: The final claim is a premise/normalization check obtained by combining Pick/Euler counting with an existing general multiplicity theorem. It corrects the stated target setup but does not add a new structural lemma, classification, or motivated invariant beyond the already-published genus-3 case.
risks: The correction is operationally useful for avoiding a false target, but that utility is not the same as a substantive new mathematical result.

broader_coverage: Lee–Len Theorem 4.4 covers every genus-3 tropical plane quartic, strictly broader than the named central-unit-square subdivision.

checked_sources.comparison: The theorem explicitly gives multiplicity one for all seven bitangent classes when genus is 3, so it dominates the final claim once genus 3 is established.
